transcript:
14:00 Jesse Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - Jesse from Redwood, Priya and Liam on the engineering side.
14:01 Aisha Rahman: Hi all, Aisha here, and Carlos and Ming are on from NovaEdge.
14:02 Jesse Carter: Great. Purpose today is to sync on marketplace listing and the reference architecture. We want to make sure the artifacts we deliver match NovaEdge's requirements.
14:03 Priya Nair: From a technical perspective, there are two common patterns we propose: (1) hosted Redwood API listed on NovaEdge marketplace with a connector and billing integration; (2) a NovaEdge-managed private deployment where customers procure Redwood as a package and NovaEdge manages the runtime.
14:04 Ming Zhao: Quick question, for the hosted path, what data residency / tenancy guarantees do you provide? We often need per-customer isolation and KMS control for regulated customers.
14:05 Liam Chen: Good q - for hosted we offer VPC peering or private endpoints and customer-managed KMS integration in the private deployment option. For hosted marketplace listing, we can surface tenancy and region info, but true customer-managed KMS is for Dedicated/Private deployments.
14:07 Carlos Mendes: NovaEdge needs a clear statement in the listing about what is shared vs customer-owned. Also we need the packaging artifact - do you provide an AMI, container image, or Helm chart? Our marketplace expects a container tar + manifest or Helm for managed delivery.
14:08 Priya Nair: We can produce a sample Helm chart and container image manifest. The runtime is GPU-optimized so images will reference NVIDIA runtimes; that is okay for NovaEdge's managed nodes. We also have a lightweight connector for billing events that emits events to a webhook or can integrate with marketplace metering APIs.
14:10 Ming Zhao: On security; we need SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML patterns for onboarding, RBAC mapping, and audit logs. Can Redwood provide audit logs and tenant-level traces?
14:11 Jesse Carter: Yes - Redwood Console offers token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route/model dashboards, and exportable audit logs; we can share SOC2 and security pack. We'll also provide a proposed RBAC mapping for NovaEdge identity.
14:13 Aisha Rahman: Perfect. For listing we need logo assets, short/long descriptions, pricing tiers, and a technical validation test that we run in our staging environment. How do we want to handle pricing - your public API pricing vs a NovaEdge-managed pricing?
14:14 Jesse Carter: Two options: we can offer marketplace pricing which maps to Redwood hosted usage-based pricing, or NovaEdge can include a margin on top for managed deployments. We should document both options. I'll send the pricing/packaging doc.
14:16 Priya Nair: The reference architecture I propose: customer -> NovaEdge marketplace portal -> either (A) redirect to Redwood-hosted API through a managed connector (OAuth + webhook billing) or (B) NovaEdge spins up a Redwood Private package (Helm + infra) in the customer's VPC with customer KMS keys. For (B) we give a terraform module and Helm chart.
14:18 Ming Zhao: For the private package, what about KV cache persistence and model weights storage? We need clarity on what persists on NovaEdge infra vs what Redwood streams from model store.
14:19 Liam Chen: We typically keep model weights in customer-controlled storage (S3) or in NovaEdge-managed object store, and the runtime can be configured to mount or fetch weights. KV cache is ephemeral but can be checkpointed if customers request; that would need additional orchestration. We'll document defaults and options.
14:21 Carlos Mendes: Integration tests - can you provide a smoke test that we run to validate runtime on our staging? e.g., a short generation with attention profile and an embedding job.
14:22 Priya Nair: Yes, sample smoke tests for generation and embeddings, plus a benchmark harness for latency targets. We'll include a small dataset and script.
14:24 Aisha Rahman: Compliance - we need an IP/ownership statement for models and mention of any telemetry sent to Redwood.
14:25 Jesse Carter: We'll provide a clear data flow diagram and telemetry table - what is sent for telemetry, what is stored, retention. For private deployments telemetry is optional and can be disabled.
14:27 Ming Zhao: About the packaging pipeline, will you publish container images to NovaEdge registry or provide tarballs?
14:28 Liam Chen: We can do both; prefer a signed container image in NovaEdge registry for managed installs. We can provide signed manifests and provenance info.
14:30 Aisha Rahman: Timeline - we want a staging integration in mid-April and production listing by late April if all goes well. Is that feasible?
14:31 Jesse Carter: Yes, that's doable if we get the artifacts this week and run a QA in early April. Priya and Liam will draft the arch and packaging.
14:33 Carlos Mendes: Marketing - we'll need a joint blurb and co-marketing timeline. Also any reference arch or RA doc will be part of marketplace listing.
14:34 Jesse Carter: We'll coordinate on co-marketing. I'll take point on Redwood side.
14:36 Priya Nair: I'll share the reference architecture diagram and Terraform snippets by next Friday. The diagram will include VPC options, KMS responsibilities, network flows, and Marketplace connector details.
14:37 Ming Zhao: One small nit - latency SLOs depend on instance types. We'll include recommended instance profiles for typical SLAs.
14:38 Liam Chen: We'll add an instance matrix with expected RPS/latency at different sequence lengths.
14:40 Aisha Rahman: That covers it for me. Next steps and action items?
14:41 Jesse Carter: Recap: Priya to send RA + terraform + helm; Liam to prep Helm chart + signed image guidance; Aisha to provide marketplace checklist and assets; Jesse to send pricing and security pack. We'll target a staging run week of 2026-04-12.
14:43 Aisha Rahman: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
14:44 Jesse Carter: Thanks, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and invite for the QA run.
14:48 (call ends)
